name: remember
description: Store important information in memory. Use this for durable personal facts, preferences, contacts, locations, projects, and reusable technical knowledge. Response preferences use canonical slots so changes replace the active value instead of creating contradictions. Persistent is the default; use session only for this chat, or temporary with an expiry/TTL for requests such as 'for today'.

category.description: Type of information: 'contact'=people (doctor, dentist), 'personal'=birthday/family, 'preference'=favorites/settings, 'location'=URLs/endpoints/addresses, 'technical'=commands/configs/solutions, 'network'=IPs/hosts, 'credentials'=keys/passwords, 'project'=repos/paths/build commands, 'system'=internal tracking, 'fact'=general info

key.description: What this information is about (e.g., 'wife_birthday', 'favorite_restaurant', 'doctor'). For a response preference, use the same value as preference_slot. Recognized legacy aliases are canonicalized.

importance.description: How important this is (1-10): Critical personal data (birthday, family, health) = 9-10, Important preferences/projects = 7-8, Useful technical knowledge = 5-7, Temporary/test data = 3-4, Ephemeral data = 1-2. Default to 7 if unsure.

preference_slot.description: Canonical slot for an always-applied response preference. Omit for ordinary topic preferences such as favorite music.

preference_scope.description: Lifetime for a canonical response preference. persistent is the default; session applies only to the current chat; temporary applies across chats until expires_at or ttl_minutes.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 expiry with timezone for a temporary preference (for example 2026-08-18T00:00:00-07:00). Optional for session preferences.

ttl_minutes.description: Alternative lifetime in minutes for a temporary preference. Do not send together with expires_at.
